corner_table_caption: Process, temperature and supply points simulated for the transimpedance application. Point 1 is the typical statistical process point, evaluated with zero statistical offset, at the \SI{37}{\celsius} on-body temperature; points 2--5 are the imported foundry skew corners at \SI{25}{\celsius}. Every figure and table in this part is schematic-level and covers only the $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$ feedback tap; nothing here characterises the other fifteen taps of the gain string.

figures.caption: Transimpedance loop gain over five process corners, measured through a probe in series with the feedback network (Figure~\ref{fig:tb-tiafb}). $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, $C_L = \SI{5}{\pico\farad}$, $C_c = \SI{500}{\femto\farad}$, \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37, \SI{2.5}{\volt}, Randles electrode with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$. \texttt{tt} is at \SI{37}{\celsius}, the four skew corners at \SI{25}{\celsius}. This is the loop around the amplifier, the feedback network and the electrode together, not the amplifier's own gain; the two are tabulated separately in Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-stability} and Table~\ref{tab:ampab-unity}.

Closed-loop transimpedance magnitude over five process corners, conditions as Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-loopgain}. The AC stimulus is a \SI{1}{\ampere} current into the working electrode, so the ordinate is transimpedance directly. The feedback resistor is an ideal element here rather than the 16-tap string, which is why the corners separate only near the band edge; the numbers are in Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-transfer}.

tables.caption: DC accuracy by process corner. Closed transimpedance loop bench (Figure~\ref{fig:tb-tiafb}): $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, $C_L = \SI{5}{\pico\farad}$, $C_c = \SI{500}{\femto\farad}$, \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37, $v_{\mathrm{cm}} = \SI{1.25}{\volt}$, \SI{2.5}{\volt} supply, Randles electrode with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$. Point \texttt{tt} is the typical statistical point at \SI{37}{\celsius}; the four skew corners are at \SI{25}{\celsius}. Gain error and INL are evaluated over the central \(\pm 0.9\) of the full-scale input-current range and are referred to the \SI{2.441}{\milli\volt} ADC LSB. These are corner figures with zero statistical offset: the offset a manufactured channel carries is the Monte Carlo result of Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-offset}.

Small-signal transimpedance by process corner, bench and conditions as Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-accuracy}. The feedback resistor is ideal in this measurement, so the deviation of $Z_t(\SI{1}{\hertz})$ from $R_f$ is set by finite loop gain alone and carries no resistor tolerance. Peaking is referred to $Z_t(\SI{1}{\hertz})$ and the bandwidth is the \SI{-3}{\decibel} point of the same curve.

Transimpedance loop stability by process corner, conditions as Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-accuracy}. Measured through the feedback probe of Figure~\ref{fig:tb-tiafb}, so the loop includes the amplifier, the feedback network and the electrode; the amplifier's own margins are in Table~\ref{tab:ampab-unity}. Gain margin is read at the first crossing of zero loop phase above the unity-gain frequency.

Noise by process corner, conditions as Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-accuracy}. The noise analysis runs \SI{0.1}{\hertz} to \SI{10}{\kilo\hertz} at 20 points per decade; the three input-referred rows are the output noise integrated to \SI{10}{\hertz}, \SI{100}{\hertz} and \SI{1}{\kilo\hertz} and divided by $R_f$, and no figure is integrated beyond the analysis stop frequency. The input-referred rows therefore scale inversely with the selected gain tap.

SOURCE: .../tb_anatop_tia_amp_ab/maestro/results/maestro/Interactive.14
5 points x 6 tests. Point 1 = castalia_pm_25 (the MC process section at zero
statistical offset); points 2-5 = ff / fs / sf / ss. Point 1's netlist has no
cor_std_mos.scs, so _corner_from_modelfiles cannot name it -- hence corner_labels.
TEMPERATURE IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS TESTS. Verified in every point's spectre.out:
TiaFbTB            37 C at point 1, 25 C at points 2-5
SlewOpenLoopTB     37 C at point 1, 25 C at points 2-5
DriveTB, TypOpenLoopTB, UnityFeedbackTB, StepUnityFeedbackTB: 25 C everywhere
The generated corner legend reads its temperature from the alphabetically first
test (DriveTB) and therefore prints 25 C at all five points; the legend caption
carries the exception. Do not let a caption claim 37 C for an open-loop table.
Block name TiaAmpAB is distinct from TiaAmp / TiaAmpCL / TiaAmpMC / ControlAmp /
ControlAmpMonteCarlo / BiasGenCascWideSwing: the block keys data/raw/corners_<Block>.json
and data/extract_<Block>.ocn, which colliding blocks would clobber. Test names are
prefixed ab_ for the same reason -- raw CSVs are named <test>__<corner>__<signal>.csv
and all blocks share data/raw/.
Every expression below was evaluated against this run with OCEAN (ocean -nograph)
before the config was written; each returned a number on all five points. The DC/AC/
stb/noise expressions are character-for-character the ones in the run's own
psf/<test>/monteCarlo/mcparam, so the corner table and the Monte Carlo table measure
the same quantity. DriveTB's mcparam expressions reference the Assembler output
`verr`, which is not visible to OCEAN; it is expanded here to its definition,
(VS("/V_OutOL") - VAR("V_CM")), taken from the testbench active.state.
Only the rf = 560 kOhm feedback tap is simulated in this run.
NO corner power table. The TypOpenLoopTB open-loop bench has a degenerate DC
operating point with more than one solution branch: the Monte Carlo p_opamp is
bimodal (187 samples 75-170 uW, ~13 at 230-300 uW) and the deterministic corner
run converges to the HIGH branch at all five points (190-319 uW) despite nominal
statistics -- a corner row would publish the branch, not a process trend. Only the
Monte Carlo p_opamp is published, with the bimodality stated in its captions.
